assumptions: The flag flip time of 14:15 is inferred from the service's own log lines. The flag provider's history showed one recent change, but its exact timestamp was not independently corroborated against a change-management record.

The investigator placed the incident start at 14:15, about five minutes before the alert fired; the official incident window in the alert (14:20:53 to 14:22:01) is therefore shorter than the period in which customers were actually failing.

No deploys or releases were recorded in the 24-hour lookback. This makes the alternative 'bad deployment' hypothesis unsupported rather than disproven: the code containing the division could have shipped before the lookback window, and that was not checked.

The defect at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:32 is assumed still present in production. The mitigation restored the fallback path around it; it did not fix the division. The proposed pull request is a draft and has not been reviewed or merged.
Recovery was judged from a single check of the service after the revert, with no extended soak period, so a slow or partial relapse would not have been caught within the incident window.
The UpstreamTimeout errors seen throughout the 35 minutes before 14:15 are assumed to be pre-existing background noise unrelated to this incident; they were not investigated.

Affected population is assumed to be shoppers loading account pages, based on the error messages alone. No user-level, session-level or order data was examined to confirm who was affected or what they experienced downstream of the failure.
The flag appears to have rolled out partially at 14:15 before going fully off at 14:16; whether that was an intentional staged rollout, and who or what initiated the change, was not established.
input.executive_summary: On 17 September 2026, a configuration change turned off a safety fallback in the online shop, which sent customers' account-page requests down a newer, untested code path that crashed. From roughly 14:15 UTC, a share of shoppers loading their account page saw failures instead of their page; monitoring alerted at 14:20:53 UTC. Automated response investigated, identified the configuration change as the cause, and put the fallback back in place; the shop was confirmed back to its normal behaviour at 14:22:01 UTC, about a minute after the alert and roughly seven minutes after the first failures. Checkout and other parts of the shop were not implicated. The fallback remains in place, so the faulty code path is no longer reachable by customers, and a draft code change to fix the crash itself has been opened for human review but not merged. Impact figures for this incident come from the shop's own measurements and are reported separately.
input.root_cause: The `legacy-checkout-fallback` feature flag was flipped from on to off starting at 14:15 (partial at 14:15, fully off by 14:16), which routed account-page requests away from the legacy path and into the new spend-summary code path; that path raises `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero` at `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:32`, so account-page requests began failing. The divide-by-zero defect was already latent in the running code — the toggle only made it reachable — so the flag change is the trigger and the unguarded division is the underlying fault.
